messages:
tina_customer_sre: Hey team — since ~04:30 UTC our Prod app started getting DNS failures for api.redwood-internal.svc.prod. SDKs showing DNS lookup failure -> downstream 502s. Can we triage?

emma_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the output of `dig +short` and `curl -v` from a prod instance? also which VPC/region?

tina_customer_sre: prod-us-east-1 VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d. Dig +trace and curl attached below:

```
$ dig +short api.redwood-internal.svc.prod
# <no output>

$ dig @172.16.0.2 api.redwood-internal.svc.prod ANY +trace
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3-1ubuntu1.13-Ubuntu <<>> @172.16.0.2 api.redwood-internal.svc.prod ANY +trace
;; global options: +cmd
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 54321
;; Received 512 bytes from 172.16.0.10#53
;; FROM: 172.16.0.10

$ curl -v https://api.redwood-internal.svc.prod/health
* DNS lookup timed out
*   Trying 172.16.0.10...
* Connected to 172.16.0.10 (172.16.0.10) port 443 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood-internal.svc.prod
>
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway

```

raj_oncall: Looks like queries are being forwarded to 172.16.0.10 (on-prem forwarder). Do you have Route53 Resolver rules/outbound endpoints configured? Can you run `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules --region us-east-1` in the customer account and paste any rules that match "svc.prod"?

liam_infra: Also run `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dnsname "svc.prod"` in both accounts (customer and redwood) — we need to know if there are matching private hosted zones in multiple accounts.

tina_customer_sre: Pasting outputs:

Resolver rules: 
```
[{
  "Id": "rslvr-rr-0abc",
  "DomainName": "svc.prod.",
  "RuleType": "FORWARD",
  "Status": "COMPLETE",
  "Name": "forward-svc-prod-to-onprem",
  "ResolverEndpointId": "rslvr-out-0abcd",
  "TargetIps": [{"Ip": "172.16.0.10"}]
}]
```

Route53 zones (customer account): `svc.prod.` -> Private hosted zone ZCUSTAAAA associated to vpc-0a1b2c3d (the prod VPC)
Route53 zones (redwood account): `api.redwood-internal.svc.prod.` is in a private zone ZREDWBBBB but that zone is NOT associated with the customer's VPC.

emma_support: That explains it — queries for `*.svc.prod` are getting forwarded to on-prem (172.16.0.10) by the resolver rule. On-prem DNS is returning NXDOMAIN / stale CNAMEs for the specific service name, so the VPC never hits the AWS private hosted zone in either account (and the redwood zone isn't associated to the VPC anyway).

liam_infra: Two remediation options: (1) Remove/disable the FORWARD rule for `svc.prod.` so queries resolve against AWS private hosted zones, or (2) Add a resolver rule in the customer account that forwards just `api.redwood-internal.svc.prod.` to Redwood's Route53 Resolver inbound endpoint (if we want on-prem to continue handling other subdomains). Quickest is option (1) as rollback.

raj_oncall: Also remember node-local DNS and nscd caches on nodes — after changing resolver rules you'll want to clear kube-dns/node-local-cache and restart pods if necessary.

deploy-bot: [incident] ticket #INC-4234 created and assigned to liam_infra (priority P1)

liam_infra: I'll remove the forwarding rule temporarily and we can validate. ETA ~10m.

(timeline ~10m)

tina_customer_sre: Update: after liam removed the FORWARD rule, doing a fresh dig from a prod instance:

```
$ dig +short api.redwood-internal.svc.prod @172.16.0.2
10.10.20.30

$ curl -v https://api.redwood-internal.svc.prod/health
*   Trying 10.10.20.30...
* Connected to 10.10.20.30 (10.10.20.30) port 443 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood-internal.svc.prod
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
"status: ok"
```

emma_support: Nice — that confirms the resolver forwarder was the culprit.

liam_infra: Action items:
- Keep forwarding rule disabled until customer updates on-prem DNS or we provision a selective forward to Redwood inbound endpoint.
- If they need on-prem to answer other `svc.prod` names, they should add a more specific resolver rule for `api.redwood-internal.svc.prod.` that forwards to our inbound resolver endpoint (we can share endpoint IPs).
- We should document this split-horizon / forwarder conflict pattern in the runbook.

tina_customer_sre: We cleared node-local caches and restarted a few pods; traffic is normal now. We'll coordinate with our infra team to either remove the bad CNAME on prem or add a selective forward to you.

emma_support: Great. ETA for customer follow-up?

tina_customer_sre: They're going to open a change with on-prem DNS team today; target to remove stale CNAME by EOD. If they need help setting up the selective forward we'll loop you in.

liam_infra: Marking this resolved on our side. Will add note to private-dns runbook and include commands we used for diagnosis.

raj_oncall: Thanks everyone. Recommend we add a small alert rule that detects sudden spikes in NXDOMAINs for `svc.prod` to catch this earlier. :thumbsup:

emma_support: Closing thread — feel free to re-open if it recurs. :wave:
